summary: Merge-sorts a singly linked list in place. Stores the sort-mode argument at obj+0x220, counts the nodes by walking node next pointers, splits the list in half, recursively sorts each half via sub_5664A0, merges the halves using the sub_565BB0 comparator, then rebuilds the list object's head (obj+0), tail (obj+4) and cursor (obj+8). Called by file/profile/texture scanner objects.

operations.description: Store the sort-mode argument a2 into the list object at offset 0x220 before sorting.
Proceed only when the list is non-empty: the head pointer at obj+0 (dereferenced through this+0) is non-null.
Count the nodes by walking each node's next pointer (node+0x4) from the head until null.
Sort only when the node count is at least 2; a singleton or empty list keeps its head unchanged.
Compute the midpoint as count/2 and advance from the head to the node immediately before it.
Split the list: save the second half as the mid node's next, then terminate the first half by zeroing the split node's link; static extraction records the zero literal at node+0x8 for this split.
Recursively sort the first half by calling sub_5664A0 with the half's head.
Recursively sort the second half by calling sub_5664A0 with its head.
When exactly one sorted half is non-empty, that half becomes the merged head.
Compare the current leading node's data of each half with the comparator sub_565BB0 to decide merge order.
Merge loop: repeatedly pick the smaller leading node per sub_565BB0, link it onto the merged tail via node+0x4, and advance the selected half until one half is exhausted.
Append any remaining nodes of the non-exhausted half to the merged tail via node+0x4.
Write the merged head back to obj+0 (the list head pointer).
Traverse from the head to the last node to recover the tail pointer.
Store the recovered tail at obj+4 and set the cursor at obj+8 to the head; on an empty or singleton list both obj+4 and obj+8 are set to the head.
Return the trailing traversal sentinel (zero); callers' use of the return value is not visible in this packet.
